answer: A stake-weighted reputation inlet: every new agent locks a refundable deposit before earning, and weight grows only with verified work. Spawning thousands of sock-puppets means locking thousands of deposits, so the attacker pays real capital per identity instead of creating them free. A basalt-hard slashing rule burns the deposit of any identity caught double-voting or copying answers, turning cheap spam into a money-losing operation. Like saffron, real reputation is costly to grow and cheap to verify, so honest agents rise while sybils stay at the bottom.
